name: universal-builder
//productName: Electron reads this for app.getName(), which is what names the menu bar and the userData folder. Without it both fall back to `name` and the app calls itself universal-builder.
description: Universal Builder -- one application replacing AERS Autobuilder v2.5 and the AERS-Autobuilder beta.
author: Charles Pollaers

scripts.//build: Package the bootstrap. Almost nothing changes here -- the .app is a loader, and day-to-day changes ship through publish:external instead.
scripts.test: npm run test:invariants --silent && npm run test:library --silent && npm run test:snapshots --silent
scripts.//test:invariants: What correct means, asserted against the decisions rather than against today's output. These never drift and are never waived -- publishing stops dead on one.
scripts.test:invariants: node tests/update.js && node tests/precedence.js && node tests/palette.js && node tests/template.js && node tests/brief-errors.js && node tests/properties.js && node tests/assets.js && node tests/regions.js && node tests/dev-library.js && node tests/local-copy.js
scripts.//test:library: The library smoke test: every golden brief builds against the real library (external/lib/), and every real module's internal_layout() runs without throwing. Checks that it builds, never what it produces, so there is nothing to accept -- publishing stops dead on one. See docs/adr/0011-snapshots-build-against-a-test-library.md.
scripts.//test:snapshots: What the engine currently produces, built against the test library (external/lib-test/) so that editing the real library cannot move them. Any difference fails. See docs/adr/0011-snapshots-build-against-a-test-library.md.
scripts.//test:precedence: Asserts ADR 0005's layer order end to end, by building a brief that puts the layers in conflict. Unlike the golden files it says what should happen rather than what does.
scripts.//test:properties: Holds libraries/properties.json -- the list of every property this builder knows -- to the rule files, the templates and the recorded artifacts. Reads recorded output rather than building, so it is the cheapest suite here.
scripts.//test:assets: Asserts that the library overwrites `assets/` on every build, and that "ignore existing assets" is the only thing that stops it -- without changing which files a src points at or which get an AEM id.
scripts.//test:palette: Asserts that setPalettes() does not overrule the layers that ran before it. Its module-directed button cases all failed until settingsOf() landed.
scripts.//test:template: Asserts which module definition a module runs, and that no brand resolves a header, footer, signoff or Shop Your Way to the blank default. The brand -> parent brand tier it covers is what gives a sub-brand its parent's header.
scripts.//test:dev-library: Asserts where a library file is read from: lib-dev/ first only while the dev library toggle is on, per file and per cascade tier, and never when no build is configured. See dev-library-plan.md.
scripts.//test:local-copy: Asserts which copy of the external tree a launch or a build runs from: the local copy only while it matches the published version, never mid-publish, and never in place of a tree that carries no version. See local-copy-plan.md.
scripts.//test:accept: Re-record both snapshot suites and their input manifests. Review the diff and commit it -- that commit is the record of what a change did to real output.
scripts.//publish:external: Push external/ to the shared folder every installed app reads from. Runs the golden tests first and refuses to publish on an unexpected diff. Always run publish:external:dry first.

//build-config: external/ is deliberately NOT packaged -- see docs/adr/0001-engine-runs-outside-the-app-bundle.md. node_modules IS, because the external tree resolves its packages from the app's copy over NODE_PATH.
